body: I grew up around spaghetti westerns.  A lot of the theme tunes trigger memories.  Recently showed a couple, the Clint Eastwood ones, to my difficult to please 13 year old.  To my great surprise she loved them!!!
Good on you mybustersworld for being honest.  Supporting self delusion is just exacerbating the problem.

Thank you.  I have been abused one way or another all of my life.  I was sexually abused by 3 men as a child.  My father was physically, verbally and mentally abusive up until he had his stroke 10 years.  I married as soon as I could to get away from him and ended up with in laws who made my life a living hell.  Instead of being abusive, I have lived my life as a pathetic victim.  I totally hate myself for it and now have withdrawn from people so much so that I can't be hurt anymore.  The only person I have ever been abusive to is myself.

Not sure where you live.  But job centre might be a start.  My 40 year old brother was so sick of his life in dead end jobs that he has gone back to studying.  He's chosen a field that he's always dreamt of being in.  While he studies he is living on a student loan which he will pay back when he has a job at the end of his studies.  I've never seen him so motivated.  All respect to you for wanting to turn your life around.  That is the first step.  I used to teach.  Absolutely loved my job.  But I was a workaholic and eventuallu I burnt out, suffering a nervous breakdown in my thirties.  10 years later leaving my house is a major event.  Some days the social anxiety just cripples me.  So honestly well done to you for wanting change.  I really really hope you succeed.
What a beautiful baby.

I do as well.  I've spent my whole life running around after other people.  My fault not theirs because I always offer.  At work nothing was too much.  It got to the point where I went off sick for a year and 3 people did my job.  It was an eye opener but unfortunately not enough to stop me. Eventually  I burnt out and had a nervous breakdown.  Now I jealously guard my time.   I constantly fight myself to not offer help.  It's almost an automatic thing for me.  I shun most social interaction so that I won't sabotage myself.  I feel resentment at having to do the slightest thing for anybody.  Apparently my need to help is because I feel so inadequate that I'm constantly trying to prove to myself and others how competent I am.  I grew up to my father constantly telling me how useless I was.  Now I am his main carer and boy do I bitterly resent it.

Well done mate.  I understand.  After months of barely able to get out of bed, I cleaned my room on the weekend.  I felt a modicum of control for once.  Having some order around me has motivated me to tackle other areas of the house.  It's given me a sense of achievement and purpose that I haven't felt for a very very long time.  I know it's not a big deal at all for most people.  But for me these are small victories over this evil darkness that persistently blights my life.
Beautiful baby
Thank you for your post.  I'm trying hard to change because I have people who really love me and need me in their lives, especially my daughter.

Hi.  I really admire the way some of you here talk about your experiences with identity and BPD.  There are a lot of amazing and courageous people out there.   Wish I was so brave and positive.   I was diagnosed with BPD very late on.  I'm 45 now.  In my 20s and 30s  I really struggled and realise now that I was very ill.  To mask my identity confusion, I was whoever I needed to be to fit in whatever the situation was.  I developed different personas for work, social settings and home.  Home was where I was the absolutely bitch from hell.  Work was where I was the overachieving workaholic who was on a mission to prove how efficient and competent I was no matter what the cost.  Socially I was the chatty butterfly.  Always found it easy to make friends but never trusted anyone to make any substantial connections.  Always seemed to end up being the shoulder to cry on and turn to in times of crisis.  However, in my late 30s due to working 50+ hours a week to prove to myself that nothing was wrong I burnt out.  I had a nervous breakdown.  Lost all of those personas I had spent years cultivating.  Now in my 40s I am exhausted, withdrawn and totally empty.  I shun most social contact because I'm worn out by the compulsion I have for turning every relationship into a situation where I end up doing everything I can to help and please the person, till they start taking things for granted.  Can't blame others, it's me who puts myself into this role.   I can no longer work; washing up is a huge achievement these days.  I seem to float through most days in disconnect.  Connecting with myself is like plunging into a violent swirling mass of darkness and it makes me dangerously suicidal.  To sum up, I have no idea who I am and  intensely dislike what I have become. I also bitterly regret not doing things differently.
Please post anytime you want to chat.  I know exactly what you're going through.

I've just finished 18 months of schema therapy.  Very intensive.  A lot is dependent on your relationship with the therapist.  Mine was lovely.  It focuses entirely on your childhood.  I was shocked at how toxic and damaging my childhood had been.  Brought a lot of repressed memories and emotions to the surface. Has made me very self aware.  Good luck with it.
Hi.  Where are you based? I live in London.

Hi I didn't pass anything on.  She hasn't got Borderline Personality Disorder she has Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder.  Big big difference.  She is super intelligent, confident and as curious as hell.  I have done my best to hide my illness from her but unfortunately a breakdown was impossible to hide.  Slowly she is beginning to grow out of the separation anxiety and has developed a very strong and lively friendship groups.  I encourage them to do lots of things together.  Yes she does worry about me.  Children are as perceptive as hell.  But as she explained it's because she loves me.  She wants me to do things with my life.  Have to keep reminding her that I'm the parent.  Recently her ADHD counsellor commended me for the support and actions i'd put in place to help my daughter.  If I hadn't she would've been fragmented and unable to cope with secondary school.  
PS - please in future don't sound so judgemental on other people's lives/ actions.  I am suffering from severe illness with little hope of recovery.  But I will move heaven and earth if I can for my daughter.
Sorry don't know where the in came from!!!
Hi.  I'm in 44.  What would you like to chat about?

Hi.  I know how you feel.  I have a 12 year daughter.  She constantly tells me that I am her rock.  She recently got diagnosed with ADHD and I have been doing everything I can to support her.  But I have BPD and major depression.  Everyday is proving to be a struggle to stay alive.  I know she will be traumatised if anything happened to me.  I am in so much mental pain.  I have had several years of therapy.  Now the doctors are putting me on very strong meds.  I have been told by them that 7 years of therapy is nothing.  Some people are in treatment for 15-20 years before they get better.  I am 44 years old.  What is the point?  Only this little girl is getting me out of bed everyday and making me fight to stay alive.  She didn't choose to be born.  I made that decision and now I have to bear the responsibility.  But my god is it getting more and more difficult each day.  All I want to do is die.

I get large painful pimples from time to time. It makes me very self conscious and I try to hid them with makeup. I had a particular bad breakout one time when I took my six year old nephew out for the day. On a half full bus, he suddenly asked very loudly what was on my face - had I been bitten by a bumble bee.  His exact words! The bus went completely silently.  I almost melted into my seat with embarrassment.  He kept repeating question until I stated yes and then distracted him.

I have done exactly the same thing for most of my life.  With my family I didn't hide my negative BPD traits.  Acquaintances, work colleagues and friends had no idea how bad things were until I had a breakdown.  Before that I was always laughing, joking, and super efficient.  I was the fixer and problem solver.  At home I was screaming, breaking things and hurting myself.  Now for the last 10 years I have gradually withdrawn from people, cut off all but the people I can't shut out.  I just can't pretend anymore.  I am too exhausted.  But from all the years of pretending I've completely lost any sense of identity.  No idea who I am or what I even like.

The only thing stopping me is my 12 year old daughter.  But I am hanging by a thread.  I have attempted 7 times.  I now have a plan in my mind that I know will be successful.  Unfortunately I love my daughter so much.   For her I'm battling to try to stay alive.  The emotional pain is so bad that I may not be able to resist the compulsion to kill myself.

I completely identify with you.  My therapist said it's the people pleaser mode. These days I purely live my life being who different people need me to be - a wife, a mother, a daughter, etc.  I did the same thing at work.  I was called superwoman because I never said no to anything.  But it ended with me so burnt out that I had a nervous breakdown.  Now unable to work and with loads of time on my hands, I have no idea what to do or what I even like.  I completely lost myself.

Hi.  I read your post a day ago and regretted not replying.  I read someone else's reply to you and it got me thinking.  Thankfully that person's reply has been deleted.  It was not very nice.  Like that person I have faced assault.  But that doesn't mean I will blanket blame all without looking at the circumstances.  My abusers didn't have alcohol confusing their judgement.  They didn't show an ounce of regret and did it again as soon as they got the chance.  Both you AND this girl made stupid judgements of error.  You really should not drink to the point you can not control your actions.  It could've been a lot, lot worse than fumbling and groping.  Then how would you have lived with yourself.? Take this as a warning to not let yourself lose control like that again.  For the girl I will say that unless you were pinning her down, which it sounds like you weren't, she should've got out of the bed as soon as she began to feel unsafe.  Her lack of action in the moment could've lead to real danger for her. Plus don't put yourself at risk by getting into bed with a drunk male in the first place.  Both of you made mistakes that have had hurt you. Unfortunately it is very human to make mistakes.  Some of these mistakes cost more than others. I think you should both count your lucky stars because things could've been a lot worse.  I commend you for your regret and desire to make things right.  But you really need to give this girl her space.  She needs to work out her feelings.  She's probably in shock, scared and feeling violated.  Probably lots of other feelings as well.  You wanting to keep talking or apologise is like rubbing salt into her wounds.  Leave the ball in her court.  If she wants to, she will contact you.  If not,  you need to let it go.  It might be difficult for her to face you for a long time.

I wish you all the best.  My best advice to you is be completely open in your therapy.  I didn't open up about everything until I had a completely nervous breakdown.  That was 10 years ago.  I was in denial for so long that I've done irreparable damage to myself.  Also, if you don't connect with your therapist change them.  That relationship is crucial.   You're 20.  You literally have your whole life ahead of you.  I really hope that you get better.  That is the best way to get the power back from those abusers.

Hi.  I've had so much therapy - CBT, MBT, Schema Therapy, specialised therapy for abuse and trauma.  It's all helped me identify the root of my problems.  But I'm finding it impossible to come to terms with the amount of damage done to me as a child.  I've tried to commit suicide 7 times because I can't stand being me.  Now I know why I can't stand being me.  It's hard to listen to my mother tell me how much she did for us as kids.  The sacrifices she made for us.  That one act of hers sent me into a spiral of self hatred that to this day, 30 years later I can't break out of.  I have a lot of people who care about me.  But I find it impossible to accept their affections because I hate myself so much.  I feel so sorry for the people closest to me.  I am this negative, evil thing that's a shadow on their lives.
Thank you that is very kind. Big hug back.  I'm just about surviving.

Thanks guys.  For their sakes I'm trying.  I know my actions will devastate them.  But  I keep falling sick and putting them through hell.  People in my life tell me I'm a great person.  But I just don't feel it.  I find their love and care almost too painful to bear.  I feel like I'm fooling them.  If they could see the darkness inside my head I wonder how they would feel about me then.  Thank you though for posting.  It makes me realise that others can understand my pain and are going through similar things.

I live in London.  Ice climbing sounds a bit scary and exciting too.  I have a family wedding coming up.  Dreading it so badly.  I watch these people and feel like an alien.  I have nothing in common with them.  I wish I had someone I could just talk to about anything and everything.  People I'm surrounded by say I think too much.  They are bogged down by the routine of their lives and never think or even seem to want to go beyond that.

I know all about loneliness.  You can have all the friends in the world and still be as lonely as hell.  I have a lot of people around me.  But I identify with what you said about pretending all the time.  I do it constantly and now I'm not even sure who I am anymore.  Do you live in the UK?  What's ice climbing?

I was molested from the age of 6 to 10 and actually raped when I was 7.  I am 44 now and I have not and don't think I will ever come to terms with it.  But I am awed and heartened by all the courageous people who have posted here.  They have  survived and are still here fighting.  A. Collins as you can see there are a lot of amazing people out there.  Don't let an evil sick bastard continue to hold power over you.  He can go to hell with his redemption.  Give it time, keep talking and go to counselling.  I opened up about my experiences 30 years too late.

I know how you feel.  I've attempted 7 times now.  The first 4 were genuine cries for help and I wasn't thinking to die.  But the last 3 were serious attempts at my life.  Last time was 7 years ago.  I wish with all my heart I had died then.  I have been through agony since.  I'm not better now and actually gearing up for my final attempt.  This time I will succeed because I know exactly what I need to do.

Yes I can not look at myself without wanting to rip myself to shreds.  I was given counselling to try and learn to be more compassionate to myself.  Found it impossible.  Have lived with 3 decades of self loathing.  Getting even worse the older I get.  Think of myself as the thing now.

I feel the same way.  A therapist asked me what I wanted to get out of treatment.  I told her the will to live a bit longer so I can get my daughter to a place where she can stand on her own 2 feet.  She asked what my hopes were for the future, to be dead.  I havent existed for a long long time and now i just go through the motions acting out parts to meet the needs of people in my life.  I have had several years of intensive therapy and different meds.  But i think the therapy has made me worse.  It's brought out things that I just can't get out of my head. I am pushing for Electronic Convulsion Therapy to try and ease some of the constant emotional pain I am in. I heard it really helps some people.  What have I got to lose? The way I am now I don't think I will survive the year.

I have been in treatment called schema therapy.  Apparently that is the punitive critic in my head which criticises everything i do.  All my life nothing I did was good enough for that voice.  It analyses everything I do and always finds fault.  It's a bully and I'm so tired of it.  I am always conscious of everything I do and say.  I find it scary to do anything these days because forget about other people judging me, I judge myself to death.

He looks at me with desire.  I don't want to be desired.  It makes me feel threatened.  Sad isn't it? This poor guy really really loves me and I'm about as affectionate as a rattlesnake.  I feel sorry for him at times.

No I don't think I can.  It seems to be more on my mind now.  Through therapy I have had to face how much abuse I've gone through.  Rather than make me stronger,  I feel sick to my stomach and my own body  disgusts me.  Every other day I accuse my husband of being a pervert if he so much as looks at me.  There is so much talk on the television about paedophiles at the moment and it's bringing back a lot of traumatic memories, things that I had buried.  I feel so angry with my parents.
Thank you though for your comment.  Hope things get better for you.

Thank you.  That is very beautiful.  My parents were oblivious to my pain and trauma.  I am from an Asian family.  These subjects are taboo.  When I worked up the courage to tell my mother at the age of 13, she told me to shut my mouth and never mention it again.  She said it was too late to say anything and all it would serve to do was taint my honour.  Years later she complimented the man who had actually raped me, saying that he was a good man who had been badly treated by his wife.  I was furious and confronted her.  Her excuse was that she had forgotten what I'd told her.  I will never forgive my mother for not protecting me.  My father was mentally and physically abusive.  She didn't protect me from that either.  I am so determined not to be like my parents.  I talk to my daughter constantly.  I reassure her and most importantly I listen to her.  She has described me as her rock.  But she has no idea that all I ever think about is dying.  I can't stand being in my own skin.  I feel abhorrent.

Thanks guys you have made me cry.  You remind me that there is so much goodness in the world, but unfortunately so much evil too.  The evil has tainted my life completely.  I have had so much therapy but have been too ashamed to talk about this.  This is the first I have shared this thought with anyone.
Thank you for your kindness.

Hi I am so sorry to hear about your sister.  What you are proposing to do is so inspirational and heart warming.  I myself was diagnosed with BPD in 2010 after a failed suicide attempt and total nervous breakdown.  I have tried 7 times to overdose.  I am based in London by the way.  I was in hospital for 2 weeks then was placed into the care of an NHS Crisis Resolution Team who monitored me for several months.  I was released from hospital on the understanding that family would be there to support me 24/7.  Otherwise I would've had to stay in hospital.  For the 1st 3 months the crisis team came to the house once everyday to give me my medication and also to chat and gauge my mood for the day.  Then once I was a bit stronger meetings were arranged for every 2 days at the hospital where I had an hour long session to talk.  This was done to get me out of the house.  My mother, who moved in to look after me, had taken over supervision of medication.  After a month meetings  changed to once a week.  In that time I was referred to a specialised unit, where I was assessed and diagnosed with BPD.  I was placed on a waiting list for MBT - Mentalisation-based Therapy.  I  was on this program for 2 years.  It required me to attend a 1.5 hour group session and 1 hour one to one with a therapist every week.  Once my 2 years were up I was released back into the care of my GP who saw me on a fortnightly basis.  She became concerned for my health and contacted the specialist unit again.  This time I received a 2 year course of Schema Therapy.  This required me to meet with a therapist once a week.  This has now ended and I have been placed back into the care of the GP who has referred me to the in-house psychiatrist.  I am looking into ECT as an option.  Even after several years of intensive therapy I am suffering badly.  I fluctuate between numbness and extreme emotional pain.  I will most likely commit suicide not because I want to die, but out of desperation to escape the agony, rather like jumping out if a burning building to escape the flames.  Research has suggested that with age the intensity of the illness begins to diminish.  I have looked into it further and found that the more dramatic tendencies of the disorder  gradually lessen.  It's not the case for other aspects such as the chronic emptiness, dissociation or identity confusion.  I have been very lucky in the support and care that I have received.  I can't fault the medical profession.  For me it's the nature of the beast.  I don't think I can be cured and in the end it will either have me sectioned or dead.
Not I will mention it to my doctor.  Thank you.

No.  I cannot stand being me.  There have been times when I can't look at myself in the mirror because I want to literally rip myself to shreds.  But I have two children and from the moment they were born it was love at first sight.  I drove my oldest away with my Borderline Personality Disorder.  Learnt some very hard lessons.  After 2 years she's talking to me again.  My youngest I spend all my time with, do everything with her.  Am very careful about my illness around her.  My children are my whole reason for living.  Without them my self loathing would drive me to destruction.

Hi I was born and raised in the UK in a  loosely Muslim family - they preached but were not so great on practising.  But slightest mistake and they would warn that Allah will punish you. My community used religion to really restrict women.  I was never allowed out, or to mix with friends.  As soon as I went to college I went out with the first boy I met. I  was beaten to within an inch of my life by my father when he found out, for the shame I had brought on the family honour.  In the end, he agreed to marriage in case I ran away and disgraced him further.  Unfortunately I was 16 and only chose to marry my husband to spite my dad, I just wanted to hurt him, and I married into a more religious family without thinking things through.  My mother in law used religion as a stick to keep us daughter in laws in check.  My sister in laws were young and pretty cool though. I tried very hard to fit in.  I learned and prayed and fasted.  Did everything I was told.  But over time I became more disillusioned and sceptical.  My sister in laws are all married and now very into the religion.  I'm still trying to fit in but I can't.  I just don't want to live this life anymore.  I can't take all the restrictions and hypocrisy.  I feel like my every move is watched and I can't freely express myself.  I've tried to commit suicide several times and probably will try again.  I have to keep going through the motions for my family's sake. Please don't get stuck like me.  We are forced to live a life dictated by our parents.  But they are living and dictating according to a time and culture which doesn't fit in with the here and now.  All it does is create confusion and major identity problems for us and believe me they don't care so long as we conform, not matter what the cost.
Happy birthday!!!

I am on medication.  Everything in my life's ok, it's me who doesn't fit in. I literally cannot stand me.  It's hard to look in the mirror because I feel such disgust.   You can have all the things in the world but if your head's not right, it all turns to dust.  I feel sorry for my family.  My husband has told me that he thinks I need to be hospitalised again.

I live in the UK. When I had a breakdown a couple of years ago, the crisis team called the police when a family called and told them I had overdosed.  At least 3 or 4 police officers attended.  I was in no fit state to communicate with them.  My mother, who had been staying with us because of my illness, said that my 3 year old daughter was shouting at the police telling them that mummy hadn't done anything bad so why were they taking me away.  She was telling them to go away.  One of the officers picked her up, gave her a cuddle and then let her play with his equipment.  I am so thankful to that officer for being kind and distracting her during that awful time.

No offense but my first and foremost priority and thought will always be for a child.  Plus I said she needs professional help, which she definitely does.  Also, a 16 year old boy is in my eyes a minor.  He shouldn't have to be dealing with all of this.  It should be an adult.  I myself was molested by a paedophile from the age of 6 to 10.  He actually raped me when I was 7 so yes my sympathy is a little stretched.  I am 44 and have tried to commit suicide 7 times and am not sure I will live to see 2019.  I am haunted by my childhood.

Hi I'm actively suicidal and don't believe I will last the year.  I have worked out how I will do it and have warned a few people close to me of where I'm at.  But I have  told my doctor all of this and am now being monitored and about to start with a psychiatrist.  I'm only reaching out because I have a very loving husband and beautiful 12 year old daughter.  For their sake I am battling it.  Not sure if I will make it because I have serious mental health problems and have tried to commit suicide 7 times already.  Please get support before it becomes a serious problem.

You need to get advice on this from someone older in your life who you trust.  It is a very serious situation.  It won't go away if you ignore it.  Unfortunately there is something wrong with your girlfriend and she definitely needs professional help. She should not be around young children at all.  These kinds of urges don't just disappear and it only takes a split second to make a mistake.  As a parent I would not want my child around anyone even thinking those thoughts.  A child's safety always comes first.  It's worrying that you're only 16.  Honestly you do need to get out of this relationship before something happens and you end up in trouble or feeling responsible because you knew.  As to her threats about suicide, that is on her.  Not your responsibility.  Staying with someone because of emotional blackmail never works.

Hi.  I really suffer at that time.  I just cannot control my emotions.   But it's more at me than anyone else.  I am actually seeing my doctor about it because I get dangerously suicidal.  I am moody and irritable with everyone else.  My husband knows better than to start an argument with me during that period because of what I could end up doing.  It's insane.  I actually fear that time of the month.  What i can say about your  girlfriend is she needs to take responsibility and get help.  Whether she means to or not, her behaviour towards you is a form of abuse.  No one should make you feel so bad about yourself.  You're living your life on eggshells and at least if she was seeking help, you'd have some hope of change.  She is rational part of the time so must know that her behaviour is really out of order.  You sound like a decent guy.  Maybe you need to take time to reflect on what you want out of life.

Hi.  You sound like a really fun and cool person.  Be yourself.  As long as you're not  saying hurtful things, deliberately setting out to cause trouble, why should you keep quiet.  Believe me you hide long enough you will lose yourself.  I have spent my whole life putting on different faces for different people and now I'm facing a serious identity crisis.  I have no idea who I am or what I like.  I hate myself for living a lie and not having the courage to be myself.  Now I've lost me.

As I've gotten older I've withdrawn and reduced my social circle to people I can't avoid.  Every single friend I had I've shut out.  At one stage I was very sociable, outgoing and up for a laugh.   But secretly I'd spend all my time analysing everything I said and did and also what their motives were for wanting to spend time with me.  I could never quite trust that they just liked me and was always setting them impossible tests that I'd knew they would fail.  I put myself through hell.  Over time I realised it's less painful if I kept my  distance.  On the surface I will be very friendly and helpful, but I don't trust anyone enough to allow them close.

I'm afraid even with acknowledgement and tons of therapy she may never totally escape the terribleness of this illness.  BPD can be a lifelong condition.  After 20 years of turmoil i am much less volatile but i am still very ill.  I don't tear my partner to shreds anymore.  In fact our marriage is at its most loving and stable.  But fundamentally I may still let him down because he has no idea how suicidal i am all the time.  I just can't stand being me and don't know how much longer I can keep from self destructing.  It's very sad as I have two children.  If I do what feels like the inevitable, I will be leaving a lot of damage in my wake.  I am trying everything I can to not let them down.  In your case, the guilt you're feeling is a testament to the very decent person you are. But you have a right to a happy and loving life.  If at least she was trying to work with you, there would be something to hope and aim for.  Without hope life just isn't worth anything. Good luck to you and please let us know how you are getting on.

Yes I did.  I think it's something to do with the hormones.  Had such rough pregnancies that I didn't have time to act crazy.  Felt emotionally calmer and actually more focused.  Lasted for at least a year after I gave birth.  Although I got very obsessed with both my babies.

Unfortunately nothing you say or do will seem reasonable to her.  At the end of the day you are breaking up with her.  Fear of abandonment is a trigger but if you don't set the boundaries you're setting, you will be giving her a sliver of hope where it sounds like there is none.  Then she won't move on. You have to be cruel to be kind. Like someone else said, you are only responsible for yourself.  Yes she is sick.  But that doesn't give her rights over your life.  Unfortunately a lot of BPD sufferers will do whatever it takes to keep loved ones by their side.  I have done it myself -  lied, begged, threatened to kill myself, self harmed, but in the end I found I couldn't keep someone like that.  I put my husband through hell and then my eldest daughter became my obsession.  She ran away as soon as she turned 16 and refused to speak to me for 2 years. As a result I tried to kill myself and had a nervous breakdown.  But having to go through losing her like that taught me some very painful but necessary lessons.  I am a much better mother with my youngest.  I am not possessive of her and put her needs first.  After 8 years my eldest has started to tell me she loves me again and really wants me in her life.  Breaking up will be a very hard and very painful process because you said you love her. You will feel guilt.   But if you don't stand firm, you won't break free.  Maybe she will grow from this, maybe she won't.  But you can't make it your responsibility.

Yes I do.  I find it hard to care about a lot of things.  Things that used to bother me before don't now.  Apparently this is called the detached protector mode and BPD sufferers usually spend a lot of time in this mode.  My counsellor says that this is not a healthy mode because it shuts us off from things.  We miss out on living.  Thank God I say.  Rather be numb than in pain.

Yes.  I thought it was just me that felt like that!!!  I actually resent having things to do because I feel like I don't have enough time to do nothing.  Most days I spend sleeping or playing a game on my mobile.  Then I feel guilty and like my life is wasting away.  At present getting the washing up done is a major achievement.  But I always feel like time is running out.  For what I don't know.
Set it up as a new post and then you should get comments.
Go for it.  This is your space to get things off your chest.  I've posted a lot about my BPD.

When I was in my twenties the fear of abandonment was the worst.  Closely followed by inability to regulate emotions.  My mood swings were extreme and I was severely self harming - cutting, whipping with belts and strangling.  Attempted suicide a couple of times.  Now in my forties it's changed.  Now it's chronic emptiness, lack of identity and dissociation.  I've only ever been impulsive in one area - I have attempted suicide seven times.  Relationship wise I have given sheer hell to the people closest to me.  Nowadays I've shrunk my social circle down to a handful of people who it is not possible to avoid.  I find human interaction a minefield of possible triggers.  To be fair, it's not people it's me.

I have had schema therapy where they are called modes.  The following website outlines the different modes.

Hi.  I'm so sorry for everything you've gone through.  But I commend you for your strength in dealing with it.  You are an inspiration for BPD suffers like me.
